layout: Three metric tabs (Visitors, Page Views, Bounce Rate) double as the hero and chart selector sitting above a single line chart, with two secondary tabbed tables (Pages/Routes/Hostnames and Referrers/UTM) grouped side-by-side below.
take: Let the KPI number itself be the tab that drives the chart above it, so switching metrics never adds a new UI element.

layout: Five flat KPI cards form the hero row, a single full-width area chart is the sole secondary visual, and two plain tables (Top pages, Referrals) sit at the bottom with no borders or shadows.
take: Use one chart, not several, and render tables as plain two-column lists to keep the eye moving top-to-bottom without visual noise.

layout: Page-level tabs (Events/Routing) sit above a labeled 'Event data' section of 4 KPI cards, followed by a labeled 'User data' section of smaller chart cards in a grid.
take: Group KPI cards and charts under small section labels so the hierarchy (headline numbers first, supporting charts second) is legible without extra chrome.

layout: A tab bar (Traffic/Traffic Sources/Search Keywords/Geography) sits directly under the title, with 4 KPI cards inside a single bordered panel above one hero chart, and three small comparison charts anchoring the bottom row.
take: Enclose the KPI row in one bordered card instead of four separate cards to visually bind the headline metrics into a single glanceable unit.
